reasons.plausibility: Deep cryogenic treatment of a stable BCC refractory high-entropy alloy is unlikely to induce phase transitions or significantly enhance dislocation mobility at room temperature; the proposed mechanism lacks a clear physical basis and contradicts the typical effects of DCT, which are relevant to steels with retained austenite or precipitation-hardening alloys.
reasons.testability: The hypothesis proposes a clear comparative experiment with defined quantitative criteria (≥10% plasticity increase, ≤5% strength loss) and microstructural characterization, making it testable.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes an intervention (DCT) that is scientifically unsound for this class of alloys, diverting attention from more promising compositional or processing strategies.
